headline: Southborough advanced a $38 million Neary School plan, funded trail and golf projects at Town Meeting, and prepared for FY28 budget shortfalls.
synopsis: In October 2026, Southborough officials navigated major capital planning, town meeting actions, and tightening municipal budget forecasts. The Elementary School Building Committee voted to advance a $38 million addition and renovation plan for Neary School after finding that a minimal $15 million base upgrade would address few educational or mechanical needs. At Special Town Meeting, voters approved funding for the Peninsula Trail footbridge and golf course irrigation repairs, but a proposed two-family zoning amendment fell short of the required two-thirds majority. The Southborough School Committee approved contract amendments aligning teacher pay with Algonquin Regional High School starting in 2027. Meanwhile, municipal departments began modeling potential service reductions for FY28 as town leadership prepared for a projected structural deficit exceeding $2 million.

top_items.title: Neary School addition-renovation plan moves to schematic design
top_items.why: Architects demonstrated that a $15 million base upgrade would leave only $5.8 million for actual repairs due to mandatory building code and accessibility triggers. The Elementary School Building Committee voted 4-0 to advance a comprehensive $38 million addition and renovation plan instead.
top_items.body: Tappe Architects delivered an analysis showing that soft costs, contingencies, and mandatory building codes would consume most of a bare-bones $15 million upgrade for Margaret A. Neary Elementary School, leaving no funding for boilers, univents, paving, or educational enhancements. Furthermore, that minimal plan would not qualify for Massachusetts School Building Authority reimbursements. The Elementary School Building Committee voted unanimously on October 21 to advance Option 3, a $38 million addition and renovation project, to schematic design ahead of detailed reviews in November.

top_items.title: Personnel Board adopts 60th percentile municipal compensation benchmark
top_items.why: The Personnel Board formally voted to align non-union municipal salaries to the 60th percentile of 18 regional peer towns. The board also established an appeal review panel with a November 24 deadline for employee job grading appeals.
top_items.body: Consultant Katy Yee presented findings from a comprehensive Classification and Compensation Study that evaluated non-union Salary Administration Plan positions across a new 12-grade structure. Following concerns raised by multiple department heads regarding job titles and grade placements, the board set a formal appeal deadline of November 24, 2026. A three-member review panel consisting of the town administrator, the consultant, and a board member will review submissions before final recommendations head toward Town Meeting.

top_items.title: Peninsula Trail pedestrian bridge CPA funding preserved and approved
top_items.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to keep the full $428,550 CPA funding request on the warrant rather than scaling back the project. Special Town Meeting subsequently passed Article 4 to construct the pedestrian bridge.
top_items.body: Facing prior negative recommendation votes from the Select Board and Advisory Committee, the Trails Committee and Community Preservation Committee debated whether to submit a floor amendment stripping out project contingency to lower the request. On October 8, the CPC voted 3-2 to retain the full warrant article to avoid confusion on the floor. Voters at the October 17 Special Town Meeting approved the measure, authorizing the prefabricated footbridge and clearing the Trails Committee to pursue crossing improvements with MassDOT and the DPW.

top_items.title: Two-family dwelling zoning amendment defeated at Special Town Meeting
top_items.why: A proposed zoning amendment to ease restrictions on two-family conversions was defeated after receiving an 85-80 vote, failing to achieve the required two-thirds majority. The Zoning Board of Appeals decided to wait for pending state legislation before making another local attempt.
top_items.body: Although the Zoning Board of Appeals voted on October 7 to support the warrant language as drafted, the measure fell short of the necessary two-thirds threshold at the October 17 Special Town Meeting. Members of the Affordable Housing Trust noted that voter confusion contributed to the outcome and stressed the need for ongoing community education. At its October 21 meeting, the Zoning Board of Appeals reached consensus not to resubmit a revised bylaw in the spring, opting instead to wait for state legislation that may allow two-family housing by right.

top_items.title: Southborough school teachers to align salary schedule with regional high school
top_items.why: The School Committee voted 5-0 to approve contract amendments with the Southborough Teachers Association Unit A. The agreement revises retirement incentives and matches teacher pay scales with Algonquin Regional High School starting July 1, 2027.
top_items.body: Following an executive session on October 14, the Southborough School Committee reconvened in open session to approve amendments to Articles 22 and 29 of the collective bargaining agreement. The changes adjust the retirement incentive program and transition Southborough elementary and middle school educators to the regional high school's salary schedule beginning in fiscal year 2028. The committee also reported that the district's current FY27 operating budget remains stable with an available balance of $349,347.

top_items.title: Regional School Committee approves revised $31.5M FY27 budget
top_items.why: An increase of $104,890 in state Chapter 70 aid prompted the Regional School Committee to re-vote its FY27 budget, lowering Southborough's municipal assessment to $10,731,901. District officials also noted a future $800,000 drop in regional debt service after FY27.
top_items.body: The Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee unanimously approved an adjusted $31,521,177 operating budget for FY27 to incorporate higher state Chapter 70 aid applied toward special education transportation. Revised debt figures for the high school athletic complex also contributed to lower assessments for both member towns. In capital planning sessions, officials highlighted that the expiration of original 2004 high school renovation debt at the end of FY27 will yield an estimated net reduction of $800,000 in regional debt service.

top_items.title: Town departments model service cutbacks under projected FY28 deficit
top_items.why: With Southborough facing an estimated FY28 deficit exceeding $2 million, municipal departments were directed to prepare both level-service and level-funded budget models. The Board of Health noted a level-funded budget would require Friday closures and delayed septic reviews.
top_items.body: Town leadership is preparing for difficult fiscal conditions under Proposition 2 1/2, asking boards to evaluate a multi-year operational override while submitting contingency budgets. On October 20, the Board of Health approved a level-funded Option B of $317,292 alongside its preferred $329,835 request, warning in a memo that failing to pass an override would lead to reduced office hours and delayed septic inspections. The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee similarly opened reviews on $2.15 million in FY28 capital requests and up to $49 million in bondable projects.
